thread.title: IBM, Abandoned By Buffett And Wall St., Sinks Lower

author: Douglas A. McIntyre
title: IBM, Abandoned By Buffett And Wall St., Sinks Lower
text:
Tweet
Warren Buffett’s huge annual convention of his investors was a reminder of his investment philosophy. He has abandoned IBM (NYSE: IBM) as a technology company of the past which has no future. He embraced Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) as the anchor company of the future of tech.
Buffett, decades long chief of Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK-B), said he no longer owns a single share of IBM. He want to buy more Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) shares. He likes its future, its technology, and it share buyback and dividend. Among his comments on Apple were “I love the idea of having our 5 percent, or whatever it is, maybe grow to 6 or 7 percent without our laying out a dime.”
Then, there is IBM. Buffett believe that IBM was among his poorest investment decision of the last several years. It is easy to justify his position. Over the last two years, Apple’s shares are higher by 103%, IBM’s are down 3%, against a 30% improvement in the S&P 500.
It would be instructive to know exactly why Buffett dumped IBM. Investors continue to crave a look at the exact logic behind his decisions. Certainly, IBM’s lack of success as it entered the cloud computing and artificial intelligence sectors are among the reasons, although IBM’s CEO Ginni Rometty continues to sell IBM’s advances. In its most recently reported quarter, IBM’s revenue rose only 5% to $19.1 billion. EPS dropped 2% to $1.81. Rometty parrots what she has said about the companies earnings for many quarters:
“In the first quarter we maintained momentum in our business, with reported revenue growth in total and across our major segments.These results reinforce that our clients value our innovative technologies, our industry expertise and our commitment and actions for the responsible stewardship of their privacy and data. This is also reflected in our leadership positions in enterprise cloud, AI and security.”
It is a story IBM management has to tell itself over and over again. It has flooded the market with advertising for Watson, the proxy fore IBM’s advanced technology. Despite an investment which has to be in the hundreds of millions of dollars, Watson has failed to make the sale
Apple has also diversified by building on its relationship with hundreds of millions of customers. At one point these people only bought Apple hardware. The company’s future appears to be Apple’s ability to sell its growing customer services. Apple has more than one future. Each is very healthy
IBM has no future at all, based on Buffett’s decision, both orphaned by him and the larger market By Douglas A. McIntyre
